title: Replace 33 empty catch blocks with proper error handling
description:
The codebase has 33 empty catch blocks (catch {}) that silently swallow errors. These are concentrated in:

- src/agent-memory/main.ts: 11 instances
- src/agent-runtime/main.ts: 9 instances
- src/fleet/main.ts: 9 instances
- src/inference-cloud/server.ts: 1 instance
- src/inference-local/server.ts: 1 instance

Fix strategy: For socket cleanup (socket.end(), agent.kill()), add a console.debug or console.warn with the error. For JSON parsing and query execution, add a console.error with context. Categorize each catch block by whether it is cleanup (acceptable to ignore) or logic (must report).

title: Standardize catch block error variable typing
description:
The codebase has inconsistent error variable typing in catch blocks:

- src/agent-runtime/main.ts: 13 instances of catch (e) with no type annotation
- src/fleet-reporter/main.ts: 3 instances of catch (e)
- src/fleet/main.ts: uses various patterns

Some catch blocks use catch (e) without type, others use catch (error), and some use catch (e: any). This is inconsistent and makes error handling harder to reason about.

Fix strategy: Standardize to catch (error: unknown) throughout, then use error instanceof checks for type narrowing where needed. This is the TypeScript-recommended pattern.

title: Fix inconsistent JSON output format across agent-jobs commands
description:
In src/agent-jobs/main.ts, output format is inconsistent across commands:

- Most commands output JSON via console.log(JSON.stringify(result ?? null))
- Some commands output plain 'null' (claim command at line 304)
- Usage messages go to console.error with 'Usage: ...' prefix
- Error messages vary: some use console.error('Usage: ...'), others use process.exit(64)

Fix strategy: Standardize all command outputs to JSON (either the result or {error: 'message'}). Move usage messages to stderr as a structured error object. Ensure consistent exit codes (0 for success, 64 for usage errors).

title: Add tests for fleet-reporter main module
description:
src/fleet-reporter/main.ts has 0 tests. This is a long-running worker loop that:

1. Monitors public layer messages
2. Batches them into bursts
3. Summarizes via inference or heuristic fallback
4. Stores results in memory tables

Key functions to test:
- shouldFlushBurst(messages): threshold and timeout logic
- heuristicSummary(messages): regex-based topic detection
- requestSummary(messages): socket communication (mockable)

The module is a single main.ts with no exported functions for testing. Consider extracting shouldFlushBurst and heuristicSummary into a separate testable module, or test via the main entry point.

title: Fix inconsistent error handling across inference-cloud providers
description:
The four inference-cloud providers handle errors inconsistently:

- inference-cloud-anthropic/main.ts: catch re-throws unknown errors (throw error)
- inference-cloud-google/main.ts: catch returns error response for ALL errors (no re-throw)
- inference-cloud-openai/main.ts: NOT YET REVIEWED
- inference-cloud-openrouter/main.ts: catch re-throws unknown errors (throw error)

The Google provider silently swallows all errors by returning an error response, while Anthropic and OpenRouter re-throw. This is inconsistent and could lead to silent failures in Google provider.

Fix strategy: Choose one pattern (re-throw unknown errors is better for visibility) and apply it consistently across all four providers. Add the same pattern to OpenAI provider.
